chunks: What was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman, from 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan, who said:

I said to Abū ‘Abd Allāh عليه السلام: A man owes such a quantity of supererogatory prayers that, due to their abundance, he does not know how much it is. What should he do? He said: “Then let him pray until, because of their abundance, he no longer knows how much he has prayed, and thus he will have made up according to the extent of his knowledge.”

I said: But he is not able to make them up because of the abundance of his work. He said: “If his occupation is in seeking a livelihood that is unavoidable, or in fulfilling the need of a believing brother, then there is nothing upon him. But if his occupation is for worldly matters with which he busied himself away from prayer, then making them up is upon him; otherwise he will meet Allah, Mighty and Majestic, treating lightly, being negligent, and wasting the sunnah (prophetic tradition) of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.”
I said: If he is not able to make them up, is it appropriate for him to give charity? He remained silent for a while, then said: “Yes, then let him give charity as charity.”
I said: And how much should he give in charity? He said: “According to his means; and the minimum of that is one mudd for each poor person in place of each prayer.”
So I said: For how much prayer is one mudd due for each poor person? He said: “For every two rak‘ahs of the night prayer, and every two rak‘ahs of the day prayer.”

I said: He is not able. He said: “One mudd for every four rak‘ahs.” I said: He is not able. He said: “One mudd for each night prayer, and one mudd for the day prayer; and salat (prayer) is better, and salat (prayer) is better.”

key_terms.أَخٍ مُؤْمِنٍ: a believing brother whose need may justify one’s occupation
key_terms.سُنَّةِ رَسُولِ ٱللَّهِ: the prophetic tradition that must not be treated lightly
key_terms.صَدَقَةٍ: charitable giving as a substitute when unable to perform the make-up
key_terms.صَلَاةِ ٱللَّيْلِ: the night prayer used here as a unit in calculating charity
key_terms.صَلَاةِ ٱلنَّوَافِلِ: supererogatory prayers that are owed and need to be made up
key_terms.مُدٌّ: a measured amount given to a poor person
key_terms.ٱلْقَضَاءِ: making up missed acts of worship

ai.seo_question: What should someone do if he owes many missed nawafil prayers and cannot make them all up?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling for one who owes many missed supererogatory prayers and cannot determine their exact number. He should make them up according to the extent of his knowledge, and if genuinely unable due to necessary livelihood or helping a believing brother, there is no blame; otherwise, neglecting them for worldly preoccupation is blameworthy. If he cannot perform the make-up prayers, he may give charity in graded amounts, though salat (prayer) remains superior.
